startup_order: Sample six motor bits/source freshness, real joint feedback and normal arm status under the existing command lock.
Send EnableArm(7). If the pre-enable sample was not already all-enabled, return and wait for later fresh motor confirmation.
After all-enabled confirmation, send MotionCtrl_2(CAN,MOVEJ,15,0) and the fixed init target every .20s.
Require position error<.015rad and speed<.02rad/s continuously .30s; only then accept the first fully checked MPPI command.

old_startup_comparison.old_order: ConnectPort(default PiperInit queries) -> MotionCtrl_2(CAN,MOVEJ,30,0) -> auto-enable loop -> external original bridge target at5Hz, whose driver callback uses configured fixed_vel15.
old_startup_comparison.current_difference: New bounded native sender owns the fixed target; current startup does not set mode or write a fresh position before enabling.
old_startup_comparison.sdk_piper_init: Installed SDK PiperInit only queries motor angle/speed/acceleration limits and firmware (lines720-728); it does not clear motion targets.

possible_not_proven: There is an enable-before-new-target window. A retained firmware MOVEJ target/mode could matter if firmware resumes it on enable; current logs do not record outgoing first target or firmware target state, so this is not a proven cause.

No evidence currently establishes a changed startup target, bad radian/degree conversion, MPPI-issued startup motion, or a firmware-reused target. The observed abnormal motion itself needs operator description or existing state records.
minimum_next_diagnostic_if_authorized: Log the same pre-enable feedback q/source age, six motor bits and arm mode together with intended target counts; log once when the first MotionCtrl2/JointCtrl is actually sent. Do not reset firmware, replay an old target, or change enable ordering without review.
